group: Signing in and the daily view
blurb: A private CRM. The first authorised company address became Management; after that people are invited and set their own password from a single-use link.
shots: The dashboard, with a day's work in it
Today, then what is in flight, then what is quietly going wrong. Every figure names the status it counted, and concluded is never added to registered.
The same dashboard on day one
An empty CRM shows zeros and says what to do about them. Nothing is invented to fill the space, and no sample data is shipped.
Typing an ID number into search would put it in the address bar, the browser history and the server log. The CRM refuses and says where to look instead.

group: People — one master record per person
blurb: One person, one record, whatever they are to the business. Business area and client type stay separate concepts.
shots: The duplicate check runs before anybody is created
Not after. The CRM looks for the same person by name, by number and by a one-way fingerprint of the identity number.
The identity number is masked. Revealing it is a decision, taken by somebody authorised, and that access is logged — the log records that it was viewed, never the number.
The same person, captured a second time
Creating anyway is blocked until somebody confirms it really is a different person.

group: Properties — one master record per property
blurb: Six status concepts kept deliberately apart, because a property can be off market, with an expired sole mandate, that was sold by a third party.
shots: Property status, sales status, rental status, mandate status, mandate type and sale outcome, side by side, each labelled.
Matched on erf and portion number, on address, and on name.
What is in flight on this property
Leads, viewings, valuations, offers and transactions, each linked back to the one master record.

group: The pipeline — and the distinction the whole CRM turns on
blurb: A sale being concluded is not a sale being registered. They are months apart, and only one of them is money.
shots: Opened from a profile, so the person is already chosen. A lost lead cannot be saved without a reason.
A concluded sale is not a registered sale
The transaction is concluded. Registration is a separate act with its own date, and the database refuses the status 'registered' without one.
What is in flight for this client
Every record that touches them, in one place, without a second copy of the person.

group: Compliance — what somebody actually agreed to
blurb: Permission per channel, with evidence. A do-not-contact request overrides every permission and is released, never deleted.
shots: Per channel, with what backs each one up. A granted permission with no evidence is flagged for checking rather than shown as clear.
The preflight, before anybody is contacted
Green, amber or red per channel, with the reason. Computed in the database, so a reader who cannot see the do-not-contact entry is still told RED.
No connection to the National Consumer Commission opt-out register. Batches can be prepared and results loaded by hand. Nothing is checked automatically.

blurb: Nothing is written until somebody has seen what will happen. One transaction, all or nothing, and a rollback that archives rather than deletes.
shots: Columns matched automatically, duplicates found, and a row with nothing to identify it refused outright.
Created, updated and refused, counted separately. Rolling back archives what it created and leaves what it updated alone — and says so.

blurb: There is no mail server, no WhatsApp API and no SMS gateway behind any of this. Every conversation here is one somebody had and then wrote down.
shots: The outcomes are what a person observed — spoke to them, left a message, no answer. There is no 'delivered', no 'read' and no 'bounced' to record.
The conversation on the client's profile
First and last contact come from the log, not from a guess. A follow-up becomes a real task, not a date in a note.
A template is wording to paste. Using one is not sending, and a merge field shows as a placeholder rather than pretending to be filled.

group: Entities and FICA — recorded, never asserted
blurb: The CRM cannot verify anybody. No Home Affairs, no CIPC, no deeds office, no credit bureau, no sanctions or PEP list.
shots: A trust, with the people behind it
FICA is largely about establishing who is really behind an entity, so until a director, member or trustee is recorded the CRM says that question is unanswered.
A FICA file as a to-do list
What the office asked for, what arrived, and what is still outstanding. The file cannot be recorded as verified while required items are outstanding.
Verified by a person, not by software
The name and the date go onto the file permanently. The database refuses the status 'verified' with nobody's name and no date on it.
The entity that owns the property
With its FICA standing, one click from the property.
Every file, and what it really means
The honesty statement sits at the top of the section, because this is exactly where somebody would otherwise assume an automatic check had happened.

group: Commission — worked out, approved, and only then paid
blurb: Three different things, never one total. Nothing is earned until the transfer registers, and “paid” is somebody's word with their name against it.
shots: 5% of 2 850 000, VAT at 15%, invoice total. Worked out on integer cents, and worked out again on the server before anything is stored.
The transfer has not registered. The CRM does not merely hide the buttons: the database refuses to invoice or pay against an unregistered transfer.
Shares that add up to more than the whole are refused by the database. What is left over after rounding goes to the largest share, so the parts add back up to the whole.
Recorded as paid by a person, not confirmed by a bank
The CRM is connected to no bank account and checked nothing. The whole history of the commission is kept, and nobody can alter it.
Being worked out. Waiting on the deeds office. Due to the office. Recorded as paid. Adding them together is the error this whole section exists to prevent.
An agent sees their own; row level security has already removed everybody else's shares before the query runs.
Configuration, not code. Changing a rate here changes what the next commission starts from and never rewrites a figure somebody has already agreed.

group: Reports, exports and the office's own settings
blurb: Where a CRM usually starts summarising, and where these rules get their sharpest test.
shots: Reports that refuse to blend statuses
Concluded is counted as a deal that may still fall over. Registered is counted as a transfer that happened. Never as one number.
A mandate marked active past its expiry; a property marked registered with no registered transaction. Each needs a person to decide which record is right.
No export contains an identity number, a passport number or a credential. Every one that happens is logged, and the database refuses to let the log be altered or deleted.
In-app only. No email, no SMS, no push. A notification waits inside the CRM until the person next opens it.
An invitation the CRM cannot send
It hands back a single-use link and says so in capitals, rather than implying an email went out.
Six external services, each with its internal architecture in place and no credential. And backups: the CRM takes none, can verify none, and never shows a green tick.
Business values, changeable without a deployment
Rates, thresholds and how long a check stays current. Changing one never rewrites the past.

blurb: Checked by the test suite, not by eye: every page is measured for sideways scrolling at 390 pixels wide.
shots: The client list on a phone
Wide tables scroll inside their own box. The page itself never scrolls sideways.
Capturing a client on a phone
The same form, one column, with the tap targets an actual thumb can hit.
Forty-one pages are measured for horizontal overflow on every smoke run.
